issues.detail: The Greek 'η γαρ ημερα δηλωσει' means 'for the day will declare/manifest'. The Vietnamese translation 'vì ngày đó sẽ bày tỏ nó' (because that day will manifest it) adds an object ('nó' - it) that is not present in the Greek structure, and slightly shifts the focus of what the day is declaring.

The Greek 'οποιον εστιν' (which kind/what kind) is rendered as 'xem thuộc loại nào' (to see what kind). While the meaning is similar, the Vietnamese phrasing adds a slight interpretive layer ('xem' - to see/check) that isn't explicitly in the Greek verb 'δοκιμασει' (will test).
